deepdive.sec: Industrial Prefabricated Construction & Renewable Energy Infrastructure

bull_bear.body: IPO proceeds fully deployed in capex (Rs.160cr); no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on capacity expansion and working capital efficiency; trade payables normalized to Rs.15cr lower than Q2
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: NGT ban delays civil work for expansion sites; monsoon impacts customer site readiness (not company operations); reliance on fixed-price contracts without escalation clauses (mitigated by weekly pricing and inventory buffers); execution risk in complex renewable cell/glass plant projects
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, proactive, and defensive on guidance; emphasized YoY comparison over QoQ; highlighted operational discipline, repeat customer loyalty, and natural hedging from pricing model; dismissed market disappointment as misaligned with actual performance
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Defense projects already executed in Siachen (300km above sea level); sandwich panels used for in-house infrastructure and sold to contractors; 14-15 buildings delivered to single renewable customer with 2-2.5% premium on repeat orders; 35-40 day FG inventory delay in Dec 2025 due to holiday payment lags, not demand collapse
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash position of ~INR 1,032 Mn, described as continuing to be strong; A+ credit rating reaffirmed.
- IPO proceeds spent of Rs. 1,762 Mn until the end of Q1 FY27 (deck's own total), against object-wise spends of ~454 Mn on Ghiloth, ~396 Mn on Mambattu, 700 Mn on borrowings and ~212 Mn on general corporate purposes, with ~*160 Mn pertaining to IPO expenses.
- Borrowing repayment of INR 700 Mn made "Without any Prepayment Penalty".
- MD states: "We remain committed to capital discipline, utilizing our IPO proceeds for strategic growth."
- Offer for sale of up to 10,000,000 equity shares of face value ₹2 by the Promoter / Promoter Group Selling Shareholders.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Structural Steel: 1,33,000 tons capacity across 3 plants; Sandwich Panels: 13.1 lakh sqm capacity; new Ghiloth line adding 8 lakh sqm (Rs.101cr CAPEX); margins comparable between PEB and panels; PEB cost breakdown: 60-65% build-up on average, varies by project (e.g., 50% in warehousing, 80%+ in high-rise)
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Describes itself as "One of the Fastest Growing End-to-end Prefab Solution Providers in India", claiming 34.2% prefab revenue CAGR (FY22-26) versus prefab industry CAGR of 8.3% (FY19-26) — "About 4.5x" / "more than 4 times of Industry growth"; overall business revenue CAGR of 35.7% in a similar period.
- Claims an 8% market share in India in EPS (expanded polystyrene) and states "EPack Leading the Indian EPS market".
- States it has "emerged as a clear First Choice in renewable Sector", with growth opportunity also seen in Semi Conductor and Solar; current strategic focus listed as renewables, data centres, semiconductors, power and energy including EV, logistics and large-scale prefab use cases "where speed of construction is non-negotiable".
- Regional strategy cited as succeeding: the Mambattu facility "helped secure about 43% of PEB revenue from South India", a model management plans to replicate with a new facility in the West serving Maharashtra, Gujarat and nearby regions.
- Customer base described as industry-agnostic and diversified across 14 named end-industries (automobile, cement, chemicals & fertilizers, power & renewable energy, cold storage, pharma, warehouse & e-logistics, etc.).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Subsidiary] Forming a 100% subsidiary to tap the growing data centre solution business.
- [Leadership] Senior leadership strengthened with the induction of "an experienced industry professional who has previously led major steel building and infrastructure businesses", alongside internal talent development.
- [Major orders] Major orders received from Emvee, HEC, SAEL and United Breweries Limited, including an Emvee order of ~Rs. 165 Cr; the deck flags this as the highest order book achieved in a quarter.
- [Industry] CRISIL/RHP-sourced industry data: India's pre-engineered buildings industry of INR 130 Bn (FY19) to 210 Bn (FY25E) to 330-345 Bn (FY30P), with the organised share rising from 35-40% (FY19) to 42-47% (FY25E) to 47-52% (FY30P).
- [Naming] The company was formerly known as EPACK Prefab Technologies Private Limited and EPACK Polymers Private Limited.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Margins stable at 10.5-11.5% range; protected by 30-45 day raw material inventory, forward purchase orders with mills, and weekly order booking at current steel prices; no material impact expected from 3-5% commodity swings; 2022 Ukraine war-induced 40% steel spike was only past material loss
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: Rs.1,500-1,550cr for FY26 (41% 9M growth on track); margin: 10.5-11.5% maintained for FY26 and FY27; order inflow: expected to sustain strong pace from renewables, electronics, logistics; capex/commissioning: Rs.56-57cr Mumbattu (Unit-4) to commission in Q4FY26; Rs.101cr Ghiloth sandwich panel line to commission in Q3FY27; Gujarat (Vithlapur) CAPEX of Rs.55-60cr planned for FY27
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Rs.1,215cr as of Jan 1, 2026; 25-28% from renewable sector; 18% from electronics/semiconductor (CG Power, Technical Associates); rest from FMCG, auto, pharma, logistics; 40-45% from repeat customers
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Expansion into Gujarat (Vithlapur) for 50,000 tons capacity (Rs.55-60cr CAPEX in FY27); export potential in Africa under evaluation; defense/modular buildings for Siachen and extreme climates already executed; repeat business from renewables (14-15 buildings with one customer) drives long-term visibility
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Revenue grew 31% YoY in prefab division and 41% for 9M FY26, driven by strong order inflow from renewables (25-28% of order book) and electronics; margins held steady at 10.8% (9M) within 10.5-11.5% guidance despite QoQ dip due to monsoon delays and holiday-related billing lags, with order book of Rs.1,215cr securing 7-8 months of revenue visibility.
